verdict.rationale: Oneleet documents service keys built for AI agent automation and MCP servers. They are decoupled from user accounts and can be limited to specific scopes instead of full tenant access. OAuth-connected assistants are additionally bounded by the connecting member's role. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, documentation of the specific scope catalog and key lifecycle controls (expiry/rotation/revocation).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Use **service keys** for AI agent automation, MCP servers, and scripts to interact with your Oneleet workspace. Service keys are decoupled from user accounts and can be scoped for specific tasks.
Grant Full access to all tenant service-key scopes, or choose Limit access to… to grant only specific scopes.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows, and every action is attributed to your account.
